issues.description: Field 'animals' in Farm: the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 108-111) requires the Farm to aggregate animals using a List<Animal> and to initialize an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The provided solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 9-13) instead declares the field as Set<Animal> (private Set<Animal> animals;) and initializes it with new HashSet<>() in the constructor. This structural mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Set/HashSet) changes ordering and duplicate semantics and contradicts the explicit instruction in the exercise, which will confuse students implementing the task or comparing their code to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem statement by declaring the collection as List<Animal> (private List<Animal> animals;), update getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>, and initialize it in the no-arg constructor with new ArrayList<>(); alternatively, if Set semantics (no duplicates, no guaranteed order) are intended, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require a Set and HashSet and adjust the textual instructions accordingly.
